segments.text: All right, let's start the weekly standup for the robofootball team.
David, can you give us an update on the product side? What's the priority this week?
Yeah, so the big thing is the demo next Friday. We need the robots actually playing a full 3v3 match by then. Right now they can dribble and pass, but the positioning is still pretty chaotic.
Okay so the positioning module is the blocker. Karl, how's that coming along?

I pushed a first version yesterday. The zone-based positioning works in the simulator but it's too rigid. Robots don't react to where the ball actually is, they just stick to their assigned zones no matter what.
So we need dynamic repositioning based on ball location. That's the action item for this sprint then, right?
Exactly. Also Micha found a bug in the path planner. Under high load in the simulator, the A-star search sometimes returns null paths and the robot just stops moving.

That's been there for two weeks. I traced it down to the occupancy grid not being cleared properly between planning cycles. The fix is a three-line change but I want to write a proper regression test for it.
Micha, that's yours then. How long do you need for the fix and the test?
Fix is 30 minutes, the regression test setup is maybe 2 hours. I want to add a fuzzing harness that runs the planner on random grids and checks it never returns null.
That's a solid approach. Put it on the board as a proper task with the fuzzing harness as part of the acceptance criteria.
One more thing from my side. Patrick asked for a new skill yesterday. The robots need to be able to intercept passes. Right now they only chase the ball, they don't anticipate where it's going.
That's a medium complexity task. It touches trajectory prediction, the motion controller, and the decision tree. Probably 3 days of work.
Let's call that one 3 days, high priority since the demo needs it. Karl, can you take that after you finish the dynamic repositioning?
Yeah, but the repositioning is first. I'd say that's 2 days, then the intercept is 3 days. Five days of work, so it slips to next week.
That's fine. We'll show the intercept in the next demo. For this Friday, just make sure the robots don't stand still and they look like they know where to be.
Stefan, how's the CI pipeline looking? I saw the simulation tests were red all of yesterday.
Yeah, the GPU runner went down Tuesday night and nobody noticed until Wednesday morning. I set up a health check webhook now so we get a Teams notification if the runner dies.
Good. There's also the issue with the Docker image for the simulator. It's almost 4 gigabytes now and the pull takes 20 minutes.
I can slim that down. The base image has CUDA 12 and cuDNN that we don't even use for headless simulation. Switching to a slim Python base should cut it to under 2 gigs.
That would save a lot of CI time. Put that on the backlog as a medium priority improvement task, estimate 4 hours.
One decision we should make. We've been talking about switching the reward function from sparse to dense rewards in the RL training. David, do we commit to that now?
Yes, I talked to the stakeholders and they're on board. Dense rewards should speed up training significantly. Karl, you've been testing this already right?
I did a two-week experiment. With dense rewards, the policy converges about 40 percent faster. The downside is it sometimes overfits to the reward signal and ignores long-term strategy.
We can mitigate the overfitting by mixing in some sparse reward episodes during training. Let's document this decision as an ADR.
I'll write the ADR for the dense reward switch. It's a straightforward decision, the experiment data is clear.
Also we should clean up the board. There are three tickets from sprint 3 that are still in review. Karl, are VXF-12 and VXF-14 actually done?
VXF-12 is done, just need the PR merged. VXF-14 was the kick strength calibration and that got superseded by the new physics model. We can close it.
And VXF-18, the goalie dive behavior. Patrick was working on that. Is that still active?
Patrick demoed it last week. It works but the dive angle is hardcoded. He wants to make it dynamic based on ball trajectory. That's a new ticket.

Okay great. Let's recap. This week we have the dynamic repositioning from Karl, the path planner fix from Micha, and the CI runner health check from Stefan. Patrick starts on the dynamic goalie dive next week.
Also don't forget about the hardware test on Thursday. We need at least two real robots on the field to validate the simulator accuracy. The last test showed a 15 centimeter offset in positioning.
That's probably the wheel odometry drift. I'll recalibrate the encoders before Thursday.
Perfect. Anything else before we wrap up?
One more. The documentation for the RL training pipeline is way out of date. It still references the old Gym interface and we moved to Gymnasium three months ago.
Noted. That's a low priority task but it blocks onboarding. David, can you create a ticket for updating the RL training docs? Estimate 2 hours.
Will do. I'll put it in the backlog with a low priority tag. It should reference the existing architecture docs for the training pipeline layout.
Great. That's it for today. Let's get these tickets on the board and we'll check in tomorrow.
